long_biography.plain_text:
Commercial fishing was Kjell Inge Røkke’s route into business. He arrived in Seattle at 21 without formal education, savings or a local network, then built a global fisheries enterprise. The decisive shift came when his RGI holding company became Aker’s largest shareholder and later merged with it, giving him control of a broad industrial investment group.

Røkke remains Aker’s chair and controlling owner, working through TRG to steer long-term investments across energy, technology and other industries. His connection to the sea also turned towards philanthropy. After pledging most of his wealth to charitable causes, he funded a not-for-profit initiative for ocean health, making marine philanthropy a durable focus of his later public work.
